To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein-resistant materials can be prepared via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization of 2-methacroyloxyethyl phosphorycholine.

the protein-resistant poly(2-metha-cryloyloxy-ethyl-phosphorylcholin) (poly(MPCh)) was grafted on different polymeric surfaces via surface initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) and that the protein resistance was improved with the increase of the grafting density.

poly(2-methoxyloyloxyethylphosphorylcholines), poly(MPC), are effective for the preparation of protein-resistant surfaces, and that this polymer can be readily grafted to various polymeric substrata by surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of protein-resistant materials for use in biomedical applications.
the synthesis of protein-resistant poly(2-methacyloyloxyethylphosphorylcholines) (poly(MPCE)) by surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization.
the development of a novel surface modification method that allows the facile preparation of protein-resistant materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the poly(MPC) grafts were effective in reducing protein adsorption from aqueous solution.
the poly(MPC) surface is protein-resistant.
protein adsorption is greatly reduced on polyurethane surfaces modified by surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP) of MPC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the protein-resistant properties of poly(MPC)-modified biomaterials were strongly related to the poly(MPC) surface density and chain length.
poly(MPC) can be grafted from various polymer surfaces to prepare protein-resistant biomaterials.
poly(MPC) is a very promising polymer to modify various biomimetic surfaces for the reduction of protein adsorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein-resistant properties of poly(MPC) are not compromised by the grafting procedure, and the method is applicable to various substrates.

the surface modification method described is applicable to a variety of polymeric surfaces, and the protein-resistant property of the poly(MP)-grafted surface is dependent on the poly(MPC) layer thickness.
the protein-resistant properties of poly(MPC) are not restricted to hydrophobic surfaces, but also work for hydrophilic substrates.
